title: Origin of animals
summary: Animals are older than their first clear fossils. Molecular clock studies place their origin between 833 and 650 million years ago, while the oldest generally accepted animal fossils are younger than about 575 million years. Dos Reis and colleagues conclude that the crown group of animals arose during the Cryogenian, but that current data cannot pinpoint these dates.

uncertainty.note: Bayesian molecular clock models and biomarker calibrations date the origin of crown Metazoa between 833 and 650 Ma.

as_recorded.value: origin of the animals between 833 and 650 Ma
crown Metazoa originated during the Cryogenian

where.modern_name: No single place; stand-in pin at the Flinders Ranges, South Australia
where.historical_name: Adelaide Rift Complex, marine shelf on supercontinent Rodinia margin; no modern polities or geographical entities existed

paleo.not_applicable: Neoproterozoic marine metazoan radiation spanning global shelf environments across assembling Gondwana margins.

importance.justification: The origin of animals founded the kingdom Metazoa, introducing tissue differentiation, macroscopic motility, and modern ecological food webs.

reviewer_note: The gap between genetic dates and fossils is a long-running debate. Claims for older sponges are not accepted by these authors. The pin in South Australia is a stand-in.
